correctness.rationale: A fixed geometric point has simplex support invariant under the group and barycentric coordinates constant on each arrow orbit. The actual admissible orbits are singleton-to-singleton arrows and independently transitive stars from one fixed label into one block; other orbits produce competing incoming edges or a directed cycle. Hence invariant simplices form the PL orbit-barycenter join F_f*D_f^{*t}. For f=0 it has no vertices; f=1 is a (t-1)-simplex; for f>=2 the standard complete directed-forest homotopy theorem and join formula yield (f-1)^(f-1+t) spheres of dimension f+t-2. The verification source explicitly tests orbit admissibility; independently checked the f=2,t=1 two-element block orbit classification (four admissible vertex orbits). General conclusion rests on proof and cited directed-tree theorem, not that finite check.
